rites.name: Alairae
rites.text: Alairae is the concept of a sounding that gives the first roots of Tirakaluta their voice, a note held so long that groves learned to lean toward it. In the Age of the first sovereign it is remembered as the pattern by which growing kingdoms first measured their own stillness.

rites.name: Syashith
rites.text: Syashith is the concept of the first hush that precedes sound in Tirakaluta, a quality of listening that gives shape to the roots of the world as they condense. In the Holy Age, temples and flame-orders are said to keep its pitch so that the world does not tear apart.

rites.name: Halarnen
rites.text: Halarnen is the concept of resonance held in the Singing of Tirakaluta, the sounding that first gathered the roots of the world into form. In the Age of Sundering it is said to be the note that rang when old bonds between lands broke apart.

rites.name: Jorerath
rites.text: Jorerath is the concept of a binding resonance that holds the forming roots of Tirakaluta together during the Singing. It gives shape to what would otherwise drift apart, and in the Age of Sundering it became the force that pulled broken landfalls back toward one another.

rites.name: Niantor
rites.text: Niantor is a sealing-rite performed in the Courts of Tirakaluta during the Holy Age, when a council of flame-priests closed a breach between two worlds. The ritual drew the burning light of the temples into a single narrow point that locked the door shut. Its aftermath left the surrounding sky scorched and silent for generations.

rites.name: Eleimwen
rites.text: Eleimwen is a concept within Tirakaluta, born in the Courts during the age of divine trials, where it governs the measure of every door between worlds. It is held as the principle that a threshold must be paid for in kind before it may open.

rites.name: Merakalsaum
rites.text: Merakalsaum is the concept of the Courts in Tirakaluta, the principle that trials are weighed and doors between worlds are set in council. In the Age of Sundering it is said to hold the bonds that landfall tore apart, and it is invoked wherever a judgment must be made binding.

rites.name: Silirae
rites.text: Silirae is the concept of the Weave as the makers plant it, a slow lattice of quiet power that sleeps beneath the groves of Tirakaluta. It binds seedlings to the soil and lets the first sovereign hear the growth of kingdoms through it.

rites.name: Elerae
rites.text: Elerae is a concept in the Tirakaluta record, the unbroken thread of the Ki Realm that ran through the Fall, the Sundering and the Shards. It is the idea that a pledged word can hold a world together when its stars begin to tear apart. In the Pact it became the seal by which the broken worlds swore to stand as one.

rites.name: Gourkurn
rites.text: Gourkurn is the concept of the wall itself as a moral act in Tirakaluta, the deliberate choice to hold one thing apart from another. In the Walled Age its orders rose and fell as their keepers bargained over which crossings to permit and which to seal. Its power is less spectacle than endurance, the patience to keep a boundary standing through centuries of pressure.

rites.name: Voraizhok
rites.text: Voraizhok is a concept in Tirakaluta, the idea that a hungry sea-wind can be bound into a wall and then unbound to cross it. In the Walled Age it was taught by orders that kept their secrets behind stone, and during the Sundering it became the reason landfall broke so many old bonds.

rites.name: Thaguktak
rites.text: Thaguktak is a concept held in the Three Futures of Tirakaluta, the idea of a branching ending that the Library shelves alongside every other outcome. It is less a being than a principle that an ending can be chosen without being fixed. In the Age of Sundering it became a rallying notion for those whose bonds had broken during landfall.
